measurement.method: Five candidate addresses sampled after every town-map cursor move.
measurement.result: Every candidate is frozen across every move. None of them is the town-map cursor.

corroboration.observation: MAX_MENU_ITEM=4 with TOP=(12, 8) is the exact signature recorded for the party member submenu in docs/evidence/party-swap-submenu-offset-2026-08-07.json.
corroboration.reading: These are stale values left by the last list menu. The town map does not write to the standard menu RAM at all, which is consistent with it being a custom screen rather than a list.

consequence: The technique that fixed the party switch -- ask the menu where the cursor is, and recognise the right row by what the game reports -- cannot be applied here. There is no observable cursor to read, so no amount of care with these addresses will produce a self-verifying fly.
what_this_rules_out: Reading the cursor and stepping until it points at the target
Any further refinement of the hand-derived hop sequence, which is guessing with extra steps and has now cost two runs

recommended_approach.name: verify by outcome, not by cursor
recommended_approach.shape: Fly, read map_id, and if it is not the destination, open the town map and try again with a different hop count -- bounded, and reporting every (attempt, landing) pair on exhaustion.
recommended_approach.why_it_is_safe: A wrong fly lands in another flyable town and costs only in-game time. Nothing is consumed and no state is damaged, so attempts are cheap and repeatable.
recommended_approach.why_it_is_honest: It recognises success by the game's own answer -- the map we are standing on -- rather than by a belief about the town map's layout. That is the same principle that fixed the party switch; only the observable changes.
recommended_approach.bonus: Each landing is data. A few attempts map the hop-count-to-town relation for real, and that mapping can then be recorded as evidence rather than assumed.

still_unknown: Whether the real cursor lives at some address this repository has not catalogued. Worth finding, but not required by the recommended approach.
